source.work: Drizzle ORM documentation, querying with raw SQL
source.paraphrase: Build raw fragments with the sql`` template so values travel as parameters. sql.raw splices text straight into the statement, and string concatenation through execute does the same.

invariants.why: A value concatenated into SQL is syntax to the database. A quote in the value ends the literal and starts a new command.
invariants.fixHint: Use the query builder, or sql`... ${value} ...` so the value travels as a parameter. Reserve sql.raw for constant fragments, never for input.
invariants.avoid: sql.raw with a constant string still fires; once text is raw the engine cannot tell a constant from input. Sanitizing before sql.raw also fires: the check is the raw call, not the cleaner.

source.work: Drizzle ORM documentation, select with filters
source.locator: where() with the eq, and, and or helpers
source.paraphrase: Filter with the builder helpers: where(eq(table.col, value)) and its and/or combinations. A raw string passed to where bypasses the helpers and reaches SQL as written.

invariants.why: A string argument to where is spliced into the statement. A template literal with ${} looks parameterized but is still a raw string in this position.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the string with eq/and/or over columns, or pass a parameterized sql`` fragment.
invariants.avoid: A where whose first argument is a helper passes even when a later argument is a string literal, as in eq(name, "x"). Only a leading string or template is the raw-string shape this rule sees.

source.work: Drizzle ORM documentation, select with pagination
source.locator: db.select().from().limit(); sqlite-core query-builder and prepared-query get() contract
source.paraphrase: Use a result bound on selected read paths. A limit bounds returned rows; SQLite get returns one row or no row. An offset alone does not bound the result.

invariants.why: On selected bounded-read paths, a select/from result can grow with the table. A limit or terminal SQLite get() bounds returned rows. A predicate covering a declared primary/unique key also bounds rows when every inArray input has a proved finite budget and joins preserve that bound. These result bounds do not prove database execution cost or index quality.
invariants.fixHint: For pagination, add .limit(n) with a validated page size. Keep valid unique-key queries: declare the actual constraint in the imported Drizzle schema. Bound inArray input with a fixed list, literal slice(0, n), or a preceding rejecting length guard. Unknown flows need scoped project evidence rather than unnecessary pagination.
invariants.avoid: The checker follows literal select().from() receiver chains and admits limit() or terminal get() on that same chain. It resolves static local imports/reexports and TypeScript aliases, recognizes imported Drizzle table/helper bindings, and checks declared column/composite primary keys and unconditional unique indexes/constraints. It excludes partial/functional indexes, self-column equality, unknown predicates and amplifying joins; a proved many-to-one left/inner join preserves a bound. Input guards must dominate the query in the same function with no intervening calls or writes. Names such as id/slug, arbitrary lists, split queries, aggregate SQL, schema wrappers and unseen database migrations do not prove a bound. Apply this optional result policy only to reviewed bounded-read paths.

source.locator: db.query with the with option, and joins
source.paraphrase: Load related rows with one relational query using with, or with a join, instead of awaiting a query per parent inside a loop.

invariants.why: A query per iteration turns one round trip into N. Latency multiplies by the list length and the pool drains under load.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the loop with db.query.parents.findMany({ with: { children: true } }) or a single join, then group in memory.
invariants.avoid: The rule sees an awaited db call inside for, for-in/of, or while. A loop that only builds the query without awaiting it is a different shape this rule does not see.

source.paraphrase: Change the schema through generated migrations, not through DDL executed at runtime. CREATE, DROP, ALTER, and TRUNCATE inside execute bypass review, ordering, and rollback.

invariants.why: Runtime DDL changes the schema outside the migration history. Two deploys disagree about the tables, and there is no down path.
invariants.fixHint: Move the statement into a drizzle-kit migration and run it through the migrator.
invariants.avoid: The keyword match is case-insensitive and reads string and template arguments; SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE pass. DDL hidden behind a variable instead of a literal is a hole this rule does not see.

source.locator: db.transaction(async (tx) => ...) with queries on tx, nested tx.transaction savepoints; https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/transactions
source.paraphrase: Run every statement of a transaction through the tx passed to the callback, including relational queries and nested savepoints. The outer db is not part of the transaction.

invariants.why: A query on the outer db inside the callback runs on another connection. It commits on its own and survives tx.rollback(), and with a small pool it can wait on the connection the transaction holds.
invariants.fixHint: Replace db with tx inside the callback, or pass tx to the helper that runs the query. Move work that must survive a rollback after the transaction.
invariants.avoid: The rule reports select, insert, update, delete, execute, run, all, get, values, $count and query.<table>.findMany/findFirst on the outer receiver. A callback parameter that shadows the receiver, as in async (db) =>, passes. Queries inside a helper called from the callback are not seen.

source.paraphrase: db.delete(table) without a .where(...) clause emits an unfiltered DELETE FROM table statement that removes every row.

invariants.why: Forgetting .where(eq(...)) on db.delete(table) or tx.delete(table) silently truncates the entire table in production.
invariants.fixHint: Chain .where(eq(table.id, id)) onto db.delete(table) before awaiting or returning the query.
invariants.avoid: Matches db.delete(...) and tx.delete(...) calls that are not wrapped in a .where(...) call within the same expression.

source.paraphrase: db.update(table).set(values) without a .where(...) clause emits an unfiltered UPDATE statement across every row in the table.

invariants.why: Omitting .where(...) on db.update(table).set(...) overwrites columns across the entire table instead of the target record.
invariants.avoid: Matches db.update(...).set(...) and tx.update(...).set(...) chains that do not chain .where(...) in the same statement.
